risks: Increasing broth turbidity may reduce transmission path length and cause signal loss.
Temperature fluctuations can shift baseline; need temperature compensation.
Chemometric model may drift as cell density and media composition change.

steps: Collect representative broth samples spanning the expected turbidity and metabolite concentrations.
Measure each sample with the NIR transmission probe and with the laboratory reference assay.
Develop PLS (or similar) calibration models for glucose and lactate.
Validate models on held‑out samples and on‑line runs, monitoring prediction error.
If transmission signal degrades, evaluate Raman probe as a backup.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Success is defined by achieving prediction errors comparable to the laboratory assay on independent validation samples; the required error threshold will be agreed with the customer before testing.
